# Plugin Skills authentication recovery: bounded implementation design

Read-only design assessment, not implementation/source acceptance or runtime evidence. No project tests, builds, lints, generators or helper imports were executed; no repository/index changes were made.

## Subject and decision

The Rust subject is commit `78aa967cc9400bb5c207441b2a78dbf7021d596c`, tree `f62fc666ade7ad6f8dbf40e889e5ec100a74e974`, in `/tmp/ocrm-source-84120837.git`. The complete `plugin_skills.rs` and `plugin_skills_uninstall_state.rs`, their relevant tests, current snapshot-admission contract, AGENTS, SOURCE_OF_TRUTH, main spec §17 and relevant module/task ownership were read. Incoming commit `370c6680b6b8c072615875d72be67ca0e45ebe45` has identical Rust/private-image/spec blobs. Its complete Electron loader was also read: `authBlocksFromFailures` now requires `errorType === "clone"` plus `classifyCloneError(...) === "user_git_access"`. This design does not restore the earlier local-I/O classification or alter that incoming work.

**Recommendation:** extend the existing private image, under `SandPluginSkillsService`, with canonical authentication refusals and one refresh-intent token persisted **before entering the external loader**. Retain the current shared reader and consumers. A persisted refusal-only happy path cannot cover a crash between accepting a validated refusal and writing that refusal. The earlier refresh intent covers this information-loss window by recovering an explicitly unknown outcome.

The precise guarantee is about an aggregate accepted by the Rust owner after complete validation and the existing active-owner/current-uninstall-observation fences. It is not proof that Electron, a remote Git operation or an already captured prompt never observed or performed anything. The current `Result<LoadedPlugins, String>` cannot prove that a returned transport error means “no authorization refusal existed upstream.” Extending that boundary would require a separately reviewed typed producer/transport protocol, not guessing from error text.

## Existing source and owner

| Exact target path | Blob | Relevant existing implementation |
|---|---|---|
| `source/host/src/extensions/mcp/plugin_skills.rs` | `2d2474e2d43425ce39f09f74d404a22957bccceb` | `SandPluginSkillsService`, `PluginSkillsAdmissionState`, `run_pass`, live import, publication/release, `SyncPass`, guard, dispose and one-shot successor |
| `source/host/src/extensions/mcp/plugin_skills_uninstall_state.rs` | `4b158b4ad3ac1987eedfefe68c8223fcba7ef31c` | Entire strict private image, exact-byte drift checks, owned staging, file/directory barriers and recovery |
| `source/host/src/extensions/mcp/plugin_skills_cache.rs` | `f395533056fd0203a68a51c51a412ff835925001` | Existing cache version/eligibility, strict staging, atomic publication/readback; no new content store needed |
| `source/host/src/extensions/mcp/production.rs` | `4c67df65f95a2f19e67b93ae8450e18a114ed3ea` | Existing `PluginSkillsPort::status`, currently cache `authBlocked` plus `uninstallRecovery` |
| `source/host/src/host_production_extensions.rs` | `08bf6b21cd9962dfee141ebee1ae61236cd5a7e7` | Fresh disk read outside binding; `install_prepared` calls retirement while binding is held; same-root Arc wins over prepared disk state |
| `source/host/src/extensions/mcp/plugin_skills_sync_tests.rs` | `29be98102d3bf4b86a841b279fc390acff4efcc3` | Real invalid-stage/rename failure, coalescing/disposal, old observation fences, durable uninstall and release controls |
| `source/host/tests/mcp_service_contract.rs` | `031f35b24d792ab18da588cc97d171989c0b6e17` | Actual lifecycle/Session consumers and the owned child-process recovery harness |
| `projects/openclaw-rust/docs/specs/plugin-skills-snapshot-admission.md` | `cfd735257b6ba538312dbd408c1133da24d800ed` | Current PS-LIVE / PR-v1 contracts; PR-02 presently explicitly excludes authentication refusals |
| Incoming `source/electron-main/mcp/host-plugin-skills-loader.ts` at `370c6680...` | `ee5773e80ccb3d3c0396566f3cc11a3669142079` | Actual aggregate producer and clone-only auth classification |

Current code already imports exact auth denials before content staging, filters warm/new Session/workflow reads through one Arc, preserves that Arc across same-root successors, durably reserves uninstall before dispatch, and releases confirmed uninstall only after cache barriers/readback. It does **not** persist `denied`, reserve an auth-refresh intent or load auth facts during fresh construction. `ActiveSyncGuard` currently only completes waiters; the observation Arc is process-local. `cache.json` cannot cover a refusal whose publication failed. Authenticated startup permits Host operation even when its asynchronous refresh fails. These existing mechanisms therefore do not close the confirmed process-loss gap.

## Minimal private image and compatibility

Keep the existing filenames and writer. Recommend payload `formatVersion: 2` with the following required fields; this is a proposed private image, not a new public schema or permission registry.

| Field | Meaning and validation |
|---|---|
| `confirmedPluginIds`, `pending` | Preserve the exact current uninstall representations and semantics, including canonical uninstall IDs and UUID tickets. |
| `authRefusals` | Sorted unique records keyed by exact `pluginId`, carrying the existing `PluginAuthBlock` display metadata (`pluginName`, optional `marketplaceName`). Preserve actual metadata, rather than manufacturing names on recovery. Reject duplicate IDs, duplicate/unknown fields, wrong types and positional arrays using the existing strict object DTO pattern. |
| `refreshIntent` | Required `null` or strict object with one canonical UUID `operationId`. Means unsettled refresh admission custody, not a permission refusal, backend receipt, live worker or retry request. |

Authentication identity uses the **existing Rust auth predicate** `!id.is_empty() && id.trim() == id`. Do not substitute `is_canonical_uninstall_plugin_id`, parse numeric identities or introduce its control/U+FEFF/leading-zero restrictions. For example, auth IDs `"09"` and `"9"` remain distinct. Uninstall fields retain their stricter existing language. Auth and uninstall facts may overlap without being merged. Duplicate producer auth entries may continue to coalesce through the existing exact-ID map before encoding; duplicate entries in a persisted image are invalid.

Use strict, separate v1/v2 decoding; v2 fields must not default away when absent. Writers emit v2 on the next explicit transition, preserving all decoded v1 uninstall facts. Keep marker bytes **exactly `1\n`**: explicitly define them as the existing initialization-marker format, while the payload carries its own version. This avoids a second two-file version migration. An old v1 binary refuses the v2 image, instead of silently dropping auth facts.

| Image / marker | New-reader behavior |
|---|---|
| Both absent | Existing legacy state; no fabricated auth fact or refresh intent; preserve ordinary eligible offline cache. |
| Valid v1, marker absent or `1\n` | Recover existing uninstall facts; auth map empty, no inherited unknown. Do not rewrite on read. |
| Valid v2, marker absent or `1\n` | Honor all facts and refresh custody. Missing marker remains interrupted initialization, repaired only on an explicit transition. |
| Marker present but image missing; other marker bytes; invalid/unsupported image; nonregular file; read failure | Existing full plugin-admission recovery fault. Preserve bytes; do not repair/reset during construction. |

This is not tamper-evident storage: retaining marker 1 cannot independently detect replacement of a valid v2 image with an older valid v1 image after the process has ended. Existing exact-byte checks catch observed in-process drift, not arbitrary valid rollback. Stronger rollback detection is a separate requirement. Never silently reinterpret a malformed v2 image as legacy.

## Durable transition table

Notation: `U` is both uninstall collections; `A` is known exact auth refusals; `R` is the optional durable refresh token. `D` is the accepted current aggregate's auth refusals. `S` is this pass's existing fresh successful-materialization ID set, subject to strict staged-cache validation. `H` is the shared admission's `recovery_required` boolean: fresh construction sets it when `R` is present; a same-root successor inherits it from the existing Arc. `t` is the exact current pass token. Every mutation is under the existing publication lock, with no service-state/admission/binding guard held over filesystem I/O.

| Trigger / precondition | Required durable next state | Live admission and subsequent work |
|---|---|---|
| Actual pass begins; active owner; no integrity fault | Persist `(U, A union retained live refusals, R=t)` before `loader.load()`. Capture the current uninstall observation for this actual load. | Register exact local token/owner/pass and preserve `H`. A clean live pass (`H=false`) keeps ordinary cached access until an actual refusal is accepted. Pending/coalesced callers alone reserve nothing. Failed reservation prevents loader entry. |
| Active clean pass returns `Err`, or complete aggregate validation rejects it before admission | Persist current `U,A` with `R=null`, but only for its exact current token. | Preserve all earlier refusals and ordinary cached fallback. Complete/report the original failed pass only after terminal custody handling. A failed cleanup is a persistence failure, not success. |
| Same returned failure with inherited `H=true` | Keep `R` and all `U,A`. | A later failed attempt cannot erase a prior unknown outcome. Keep plugin admissions closed; do not relabel unknown as auth denial. |
| Current valid aggregate, `H=false` | Immediately import `D` into live denial; persist `(U, A union D, R=null)` **before** fallible cache staging. Do not remove earlier `A` on success yet. | Once accepted identity is known, unrelated cached controls remain available. If persistence fails, stop this pass before cache publication. Crash before this transition leaves the earlier `R`, therefore unknown on recovery. |
| Current valid aggregate, `H=true` | Import and persist `A union D`, retaining `R=t`. | Fresh results may narrow future admission, but absence of a current denial is not proof that the lost earlier result was permissive. Keep `H` until a safe replacement cache and durable completion exist. |
| Stage/rename/readback fails after the preceding transition | No positive removal from `A` or `U`, no clearing inherited unknown. | Preserve old materialized files. Failed pre-rename staging preserves old cache bytes; post-rename failure may leave new bytes visible and must not roll them back. |
| Successful normal publication, `H=false` | After cache file/dir barriers and strict readback: remove from `A` only exact IDs in `S` not currently denied. Preserve pending uninstall; confirmed uninstall release keeps its existing freshness/pending rules. | Remove live auth facts only after corresponding durable release succeeds. Current denial wins over simultaneous success. Zero-Skill success still follows this ordering. |
| Successful recovery publication, `H=true` | First publish a strictly valid cache made **only from fresh successful records**, excluding all prior-cache fallback for this recovery pass. After its barriers/readback, atomically apply the permitted exact-ID releases and `R=null`. | Then set `H=false`. This permits successfully refreshed control IDs without needing a second per-ID unknown database. Old unresolved cached rows are absent, not granted. Preserve their files on partial recovery; future exposure requires fresh materialization. |
| Uninstall reserve/settle while refresh exists | Perform current uninstall transition, preserving `A,R`. | Existing uninstall observation changes fence old success. A superseded clean pass may terminally clear only its own intent using the **current** `U,A`, because its result is no longer admissible; it cannot publish or release any fact from the stale aggregate. Inherited unknown remains. |
| Fresh process sees `R != null` | No read-time write. | Set `H=true`; deny plugin Skills through the existing reader until the recovery path above succeeds. User/managed workflows remain governed by their existing owners. Never auto-replay an uninstall or invent an auth refusal. |

The recovery-only omission of fallback is necessary for this minimal one-token scheme. Clearing `H` after an ordinary partial snapshot that retained old fallback could resurrect exactly the lost refusal. The normal clean partial/offline path must keep its existing fallback behavior. Preserve known `A` for absent IDs until exact fresh success, as PS-LIVE already requires; omission from a listing alone is not an auth release.

## Write failures and the unavoidable information boundary

The private writer currently returns `String`, and `persist_uninstall_transition` converts every failure into a global recovery fault. Reusing that indiscriminately for auth would hide all controls even when the exact refusal and the disk alternatives remain known. Keep existing uninstall failure semantics, but add a narrow internal auth-write outcome classification:

- Under the same publication lock, strictly reread after an auth-write error. Only byte-for-byte **the expected image** or **this operation's exact candidate image/allowed initialization-marker intermediate** counts as known. Preserve the observed expected bytes for the next transition. A semantic-equivalent foreign rewrite is still drift. A readback is not a substitute for the failed durability barrier.
- With a known image, retain the adverse live state and the known local pass disposition; return a fixed persistence error and do not continue loader entry, publication, pruning or positive release for that failed step. A clean pass that accepted refusal 9 continues to deny 9 and permit otherwise eligible 10. A pass with inherited `H` continues to deny all plugin Skills. The next explicit current-owner transition may retry; there is no automatic remote replay.
- If neither exact image can be established, or any state is unreadable/corrupt/drifted, use the existing full recovery-fault latch. Do not replace unknown bytes. A fresh owner after valid repair is the existing recovery boundary.

The important crash cuts are distinct:

| Cut | Fresh-process interpretation |
|---|---|
| Intent write fails before loader entry, old exact image remains | No new observation occurred. Preserve its prior admission. Loader-call count must be zero. |
| Intent is visible, process ends before loader/aggregate/outcome settlement | Unknown. This can conservatively block plugins even if the loader never ran. |
| Refusal 9 accepted, process ends before its outcome write, or failed outcome write leaves old intent | Unknown; both 9 and 10 may need blocking because the identity was not durably preserved. Claiming continued 10 availability at this cut would guess the lost result. |
| Refusal 9 is durably recorded, later content staging/rename fails | Exact 9 denied after restart; unrelated 10 remains available from valid old cache. |
| Cache commit/readback succeeded, positive journal release fails before becoming visible | Earlier refusal/unknown persists. Live and fresh owners retain it. |
| Cache commit/readback succeeded, positive journal image became visible, then directory sync/readback returns an error | Live owner still returns failure and retains adverse admission. A fresh owner may read either the earlier refusal or the completed positive image. The latter is safe because its corresponding cache crossed its barriers first. Do **not** promise that every failed release remains denied after restart, roll back the visible journal, or report the operation durable-success on the error path. |

“Known returned failure” here means no authoritative aggregate was admitted by the Rust owner. It does not mean known absence of remote effects. Treating every returned `String` error as a permanent global auth block would break existing ordinary offline cache behavior; treating a *recovered* intent as such a harmless error would reopen the defect.

## Disposal, handoff, coalescing and lock rules

Use the narrower design discussed with root: no composition change and no filesystem I/O in retirement/disposal. In shared admission, retain `recovery_required` plus local current-token/owner identity and a known-fenced disposition.

1. Under `P`, briefly mark the service disposed/retired and drop queued work using the existing service-state lock. Release that guard before briefly changing admission. Fence the exact old token so no later aggregate from that owner can be accepted. Preserve all known auth/uninstall facts and the existing `H`. A clean fenced pass does **not** make every cached plugin unavailable. Keep existing healthy `dispose`/queued-return/current assertions.
2. `retire_for_replacement` is presently called while `PluginSkillsBinding` is held. Its no-I/O property is essential. A same-root successor inherits the same reader, precise live refusals, `H=false/true` and known-fenced disposition. Do not derive `H` again merely from the shared durable token or substitute the previously prepared disk reader.
3. A new actual successor pass can durably replace the known-fenced old token under its own `P`, retaining live facts and `H`. Replacing a token never changes `H=true` to false. The old guard, old `dispose()` and late callback may touch only an exact still-owned token; after replacement they are no-ops against successor custody. Avoid old/new publication mutexes becoming simultaneous writers of the shared image.
4. A same-root handoff need not immediately flush its known fence. **Compatibility limit:** if the process exits before a later successful transition clears/replaces-and-settles the token, fresh startup conservatively sees unknown. This includes a graceful shutdown while a refresh was fenced, not only a crash. Same-process healthy cached availability remains intact. A requirement to preserve offline availability across *all* such graceful restarts would need an explicit current-owner durable shutdown settlement outside binding, and is outside this narrower slice.
5. Coalesced callers share the existing pass outcome; only the actual worker reserves an intent. Disposed queued callers return live-filtered current records. Do not reserve for the queued slot, invoke a loader in the guard, or add a scheduler. Guard cleanup must be exact-token checked: loader panic before known outcome leaves unresolved custody; reporter panic after a fully settled pass must not recreate unknown or corrupt a successor token. Preserve waiter completion and existing recursion refusal.
6. Keep the existing uninstall observation as its own fence, or thread an updated observation explicitly if refactoring it. An auth reservation/outcome write must not accidentally invalidate its own pass. The simplest choice is not to advance the uninstall epoch for auth-only journal changes; real uninstall transitions and integrity faults keep advancing it. Every journal write clones current `U`, not the pass's old reservation copy.
7. Pending uninstall tickets still cannot be cleared by any fresh sync, unknown recovery or auth release, and still suppress pruning. No uninstall replay. A current auth success may remove an auth fact under its existing rules while an independent pending uninstall continues denying the same ID. Do not collapse these facts into one reason or apply uninstall canonical-ID rules to auth.

Callbacks, clocks, loader calls and reporters remain outside locks. Cache publication/readback and durable positive release stay within the existing publication interval. Ordinary dispose after an already completed commit keeps its currently permitted cleanup/report behavior; replacement continues to fence predecessor cleanup.

## Minimal allowed implementation slice and causal Actions oracles

Production changes can remain in `plugin_skills.rs` and its existing private `plugin_skills_uninstall_state.rs`; `production.rs` needs only the existing status projection extension. Reuse the existing `PluginAuthBlock` and cache writer. Add no new command, permission service, database, market or content store. Keep Session/workflow/Runner consumer code unchanged unless a concrete assertion exposes a missing reader. No Electron loader edits are needed for this design.

Status should expose known live/durable auth refusals even when the cache still contains its earlier empty `authBlocked` list. Unknown refresh recovery must have a separate fixed status/fault representation, not a fabricated auth-block record or uninstall receipt. Healthy empty status remains compatible. Count actual admission release once in `changed`; routine reserve/clear churn is not a user-visible permission change.

Use the existing sync/private-image unit modules and `mcp_service_contract.rs` owned process harness; extend the existing actual workflow command/prompt oracle where needed. Their current full-module/test-target Actions selections already execute such additions. Add narrow named-positive requirements to `.github/workflows/rust-desktop-runtime.yml` only as needed to prove these particular tests actually ran; do not extend general governance.

Required causal oracles:

- **Old defect and repaired known identity:** seed real allowed 9/10 records and bytes, accept auth refusal 9, cause the existing real invalid-stage failure using plugin 10's relative path, then terminate the owner process. A genuinely separate process opens fresh Session/workflow owners and uses the real reader with a failed/offline loader. Assert 9 absent from get/list/update, run-now/reference and actual provider-message construction; 10 and user/managed controls remain usable; exact old content bytes/materialized files remain. The pre-extension implementation must exhibit 9 resurrection at this cut. Same-Arc reopening is not this oracle.
- **Write-ahead causality:** independently cut after durable reservation/before loader entry and after validated refusal import/before refusal-image write. Fresh process must expose unknown and deny plugin admissions, with user/managed controls intact. A known intent-reservation failure must assert zero loader calls. Do not fake restart by merely constructing a new reader over the same Arc.
- **Failure classification:** exercise expected-image-preserved refusal-write failure, candidate-image-visible failure and unreadable/foreign image. Require precise live 9 denial with 10 control only where the exact known-state preconditions hold. Preserve bytes; do not treat an injected barrier error as real platform power-loss evidence.
- **Positive release ordering:** prove a failed positive cache stage/rename cannot release `A`; then force journal release failure after real cache barriers/readback. Test before-release and visible-after-release cuts separately, inspecting actual stored bytes and a separate fresh process. A zero-Skill success and a later full success release only the exact fresh ID, with current denial winning and one truthful changed event.
- **Compatibility and recovery:** valid v1/absent legacy with a returned offline error preserves eligible cached controls; malformed aggregate does not cherry-pick its otherwise valid refusal. Recovered unknown followed by another error remains unknown. Partial recovery must omit unresolved fallback while allowing freshly successful control 10 only after the durable completion. Ordinary clean partial refresh retains fallback. Validate v2 strict fields/IDs/tickets, legacy/unmarked input, initialized-image loss, marker 2 rejection and exact-byte drift without destructive repair.
- **Lifecycle preservation:** keep the current healthy active/queued `dispose` assertions, same-root shared-reader controls, old-runtime repeated disposal, report/clock reentrancy and old-cleanup fence. Block an old loader, replace it, reserve a new successor token, then release/panic/finish/dispose the old owner: its guard cannot alter new bytes or `H`. Include the documented fresh-process conservative unknown after an unflushed known fence. Pending uninstall tickets and their exact operation IDs survive all these paths; no backend replay or prune while pending.

The owned child harness must retain nonce/parent/PID/root/phase checks, distinct child PIDs and exact-process cleanup. Fixtures must drive the actual loader -> validation -> durable transition -> cache -> reader -> Session/prompt chain; source-string assertions or test-only denial insertion do not establish that chain.

## Authority and remaining limits

Root needs a narrow PS-AUTH-RECOVERY amendment before code: PR-02's current no-auth-persistence clause, v2 migration/marker semantics, the admitted-result boundary, returned-error versus recovered-unknown policy, recovery-only no-fallback rule, exact positive-release ordering, status meaning and the unflushed known-fence restart limit. This does not authorize changing global acceptance flags or replacing fixed U.

Fixed U remains `1440bb1771372334bea23d7642bb52deb7db1845`, tree `90c8aab39972da11cfad220361781d49e1bc6700`. Exact full API source copies are available for root's direct read, with `git hash-object` matching API metadata:

- `/tmp/next-mcp-fixed-u-1440bb/src/skills/loading/plugin-skills.ts` — `19fcb97b484bbe4b199324c69cc86eef4d3235a4`.
- `/tmp/next-mcp-fixed-u-1440bb/src/plugins/plugin-root-contributions.ts` — `614b703b81889b048f43efd67d260e398cf86131`.
- `/tmp/next-mcp-fixed-u-1440bb/src/plugins/config-activation-shared.ts` — `f1d6c806adab30da1f194b90482b056953803c38`.

These establish effective configuration/enablement checks before contributing plugin skill roots. They do not define Fabushi's authentication-refusal journal or make this its upstream implementation. No necessary source location for this bounded design is unreadable. The incoming general loader/cache patches were not accepted or comprehensively reviewed by this assessment.

Remaining review is the integrated exact-tree state machine, lock/token lifetime and causal oracle review followed by the required exact-H Actions evidence. No such evidence was produced here. Existing non-Unix directory-barrier limits, arbitrary image rollback, multiple independent processes writing the same root, account/backend incarnation changes after the aggregate, remote quiescence, previously captured prompts/effects and real ecosystem/platform acceptance remain outside the claim. This slice closes accepted auth-refusal loss across the declared process boundaries without promising effects can be retracted or unknown identity can be reconstructed.

## 2. Poisoned admission and successor construction

### Observed failure

The original log at 51275–51282 contains two panics with different meanings:

The lifecycle has been permanently disposed/claimed, but the poisoned admission object and its disk state have not been replaced or repaired. There is no extra loader call on this path. The poisoned active refresh also refuses before observation: `run_pass` calls `begin_refresh` before `loader.load`, and `begin_refresh` fails acquiring the admission mutex before it can clone or persist the reservation. Three requirements resolve the apparent conflict:

```rust

    Err(error) => assert_eq!(error, "plugin skills live admission poisoned"),
```


## 3. Permission and durable-result analysis

### Reservation and admissible results

`begin_refresh` reserves a fresh canonical UUID under the existing publication mutex before `loader.load()` is entered. It clones the current durable state and retained live refusals into the candidate image, rejects an unfenced active refresh, and records the owner/token only after reservation succeeds (`plugin_skills.rs:687–732`). `run_pass` creates the refresh guard before the test hook or actual loader invocation (`1254–1267`). Queued/joined callers do not call this function until they actually become the worker, so their mere existence does not manufacture durable operations.

The permission distinction is explicit: the pending token itself does not deny cached plugins in a healthy live process, whereas fresh construction with an unresolved token sets `recovery_required`. A loader error or invalid aggregate reaches `settle_unadmitted_refresh`, which operates on the current durable image and the exact owned token. An inherited unknown cannot be cleared by that path. A current valid aggregate must pass whole-aggregate validation, active-owner checks, the current uninstall observation, and exact refresh custody before any returned auth refusal is imported (`774–817,983–1017,1254–1295`). These checks prevent a stale result from becoming a grant or a newly imported refusal after its authority has changed.

### Negative publication precedes content work

The aggregate's current refusals are first inserted into the shared live reader under the publication interval. The operation becomes a known result, then the writer merges all retained refusals into the durable image before any cache serialization or staging (`983–1037`). A healthy pass clears its token in this same negative transition. A recovery-required pass keeps its token until positive recovery completes.

This order is material to the target repair. If the subsequent content stage or rename fails, fresh construction reads the durable precise refusal even while the previous content cache remains allowed-looking. The live reader combines auth refusal, uninstall reasons, integrity fault, and unknown-outcome state; it is not dependent on raw cache `authBlocked` fields having already changed (`426–439,499–520,915–930`). Unrelated plugins and the separately owned user/managed workflows remain available when the only adverse fact is a precise refusal.

### Positive release and partial recovery

Fresh-success identities derive from the actual current materialized aggregate, including a valid materialized plugin with zero Skills. Current denial wins. Previous-cache fallback is explicitly disabled for every recovery-required pass, while the established clean partial-refresh fallback remains (`1311–1354`). Thus publishing only a fresh plugin 10 during unknown recovery cannot reopen an unresolved old plugin 9 merely because the old row is still in the previous cache.

`publish_snapshot_if_active` checks the active service and uninstall observation, performs cache publication and strict readback, then builds the durable positive transition (`1039–1095`). It removes an auth refusal only for an exact fresh successful ID without current denial. Pending uninstall entries are never removed; confirmed uninstall release retains its existing transition semantics. Unknown recovery requires the exact refresh token and clears that token durably before clearing the live unknown (`1082–1114`). Live refusals are removed only after the relevant durable transition succeeds.

The changed-event computation includes real refusal release or unknown-to-known restoration, and otherwise compares the committed permission-relevant projection. Ordinary healthy reserve/settle churn does not enter that comparison. Pending uninstall identities are excluded from both reporting sides using the publication-time captured pending set (`1103–1120,1406–1428`). This is consistent with the amended contract without turning raw content bytes into admission authority.

### Failed writes retain their specific meaning

The pre-existing uninstall writer keeps its full-fault error semantics and observation change (`628–653`). The new auth wrapper is deliberately separate: on write failure it calls `inspect_failed_auth_publication`, retains adverse live facts, returns a fixed error, and accepts a new expected disk image only if the strict reread is one of the operation's two byte-exact possibilities (`658–685`). Any unknown, malformed, unreadable, missing-initialized, nonregular, or foreign-byte result latches the recovery fault and advances the uninstall observation.

The low-level inspection distinguishes exact old bytes from this operation's exact encoded candidate, including the permitted initialization-marker intermediate (`plugin_skills_uninstall_state.rs:317–341`). Semantic equality is not used as replacement authority. The caller does not roll back, retry the failed transition, continue into content publication, or clear adverse live state on the strength of this reread.

Two apparently asymmetric outcomes are intentional and supported by the contract, rather than defects:

- A known failed negative write may leave precise live refusal 9 while a fresh process sees only the older durable intent and blocks both 9 and 10.
- After content barriers, a positive image can become visible before a later journal barrier/readback error. The live operation remains failed and refused, while a fresh owner reading that completed positive image can safely admit the corresponding already-published content.

The source does not label either reread as proof that a failed durability barrier actually succeeded.

## 4. v1/v2 schema, recovery, and filesystem treatment

The extension stays within the existing private image and marker. `StoredAdmissionImage` adds exactly the declared v2 fields, while the legacy DTO remains exact and independently version-checked. Object-only wrappers retain duplicate/unknown-field rejection and reject positional arrays. The custom nullable `StoredRefreshIntent` is required, so omission is not silently treated as `None`. IDs retain their separate auth and uninstall predicates; refresh UUID validation also excludes collision with pending uninstall operation IDs (`plugin_skills_uninstall_state.rs:45–225`).

Encoding uses the ordered state maps/sets, preserves actual auth display metadata, and emits v2 on explicit transitions. Reading v1 yields empty auth and no refresh intent without rewriting it. Construction keeps the original absent-both legacy case, valid-unmarked-image authority, and fail-closed invalid/missing-initialized cases. The initialization marker remains `1\n` independently of payload version (`228–274`). The old strict v1 shape does not accept a v2 payload.

The persistence path retains exact accepted bytes and performs read-before-replace checks around preparation. Staged image/marker files are created uniquely, written and synced, renamed, and followed by the relevant directory barrier; successful publication is checked again. File reads reject nonregular objects and retain the existing Unix no-follow/nonblocking and identity checks and Windows reparse handling (`279–311,350–479`). Stage cleanup relinquishes ownership after rename so an error after visibility does not delete the published image.

These are source observations about the implemented barriers. This review does not claim real power-loss behavior, arbitrary valid-image rollback detection, hostile cross-process compare-and-swap, or all-platform filesystem equivalence. Those are explicitly outside the bounded AR contract and were not promoted to findings merely because stronger guarantees could be imagined.

## 5. Owner lifetime, locks, panic, and recovery

Refresh identity is both owner-specific and token-specific in the shared admission state. A same-root successor receives the existing reader Arc, while its own service gets a new owner identity and publication mutex. The old owner is retired once under its publication interval before the successor can assume that shared state (`plugin_skills.rs:523–540,734–750,868–900`).

Dispose and retirement drop the service-state guard before touching admission, fence only their own refresh, and perform no filesystem I/O. This makes the existing binding-lock handoff safe with respect to the new journal work. Preparation that loads a fresh service from disk occurs outside the binding guard; same-root handoff deliberately inherits the current shared state instead of replacing it with that prepared disk snapshot (`host_production_extensions.rs:466–581`).

The old guard checks owner/token and fenced disposition before changing recovery state. Late old results first encounter the disposed-owner boundary, and repeated old dispose cannot fence a successor's token. A clean fenced token preserves same-process cache availability; an inherited unknown remains unknown. If the process ends before a later explicit transition settles the token, a fresh process conservatively starts unknown. This is the stated lifetime contract, including graceful shutdown in that window (`plugin_skills.rs:741–817,936–946`; spec AR-07).

Uninstall observation fencing remains separate from auth-only reserve/settle changes. Real uninstall transitions and integrity failures still invalidate old aggregate authority; ordinary auth writes do not. A stale clean result may settle only its exact custody using current facts, but cannot import its aggregate or publish content. Positive publication and pruning recheck the observation, and pending uninstall suppresses pruning (`983–1009,1046–1068,1123–1162`).

On loader unwind, the refresh guard marks unresolved owned custody unknown, and the existing active-pass guard completes the shared pass with an error so coalesced waiters are not stranded. Reporter panic after a settled publication does not re-create a token that has already been cleared. The inspected paths keep service-state/admission/result locks off loader calls, clock calls, journal/cache I/O, and external callbacks. The publication mutex intentionally serializes the state-changing filesystem interval; this is distinct from keeping a reader-state lock across I/O (`385–481,752–772,1164–1283`).

The shipping shutdown path disposes the plugin service before joining polling, with the startup state lock released. That preserves the established rule that queued syncs are retired instead of beginning a new load merely to finish shutdown (`extension.rs:174–199`).
